description: run.sh's real-order branch will fire MULTIPLE real orders for the SAME trading window instead of the intended ONE. decide.py's `_already_traded_window` idempotency guard only controls whether a row is APPENDED to paper-positions.jsonl (setting out['recorded']=false when a window was already traded, decide.py:173-175) — but decide.py still populates token_id/side/price/stake_usdc in its printed decision UNCONDITIONALLY (decide.py:164-166) regardless of the `recorded` flag. run.sh's execute-branch (run.sh:26-31) extracts token_id/side/price/stake from that JSON and only checks that TOK and SIDE are non-empty (run.sh:30) — it never inspects `recorded`. Per SKILL.md the cron fires run.sh 'every ~1 min during a window' (a window is 5 min), so once DRY_RUN=false/EARN_MODE=execute/gate PASS are live, a single momentum signal that persists across the window (very likely, since BTC momentum doesn't reset every minute) will cause order.py to be invoked and POST A REAL ORDER on every single cron tick of that window (~5x), not once. This is uncontrolled real-money order duplication.

evidence.snippet:
if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "false" ] && [ "$EARN_MODE" = "execute" ] && [ "$PM_PAPER_PASS" = "1" ]; then
  TOK=$(...)
  SIDE=$(...)
  ...
  if [ -n "$TOK" ] && [ "$SIDE" != "" ]; then
    "$PY" "$HERE/order.py" "$TOK" "$PRICE" "$STAKE" "$SIDE"; exit 0
  fi
